Retirement Hints From the Champion

Reigning UFC welterweight champion Islam Makhachev has indicated that his professional mixed martial arts career is nearing its conclusion. On Friday night, the Russian fighter stated on X that his upcoming bout will be "one of the last" of his career.

Makhachev holds an official record of 29 wins and one loss. In August, he defended his welterweight title by defeating Ireland’s Ian Machado Garry via unanimous decision in the main event of UFC 330 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. This victory extended his winning streak to 17 consecutive fights, surpassing Anderson Silva's previous record of 16 consecutive wins set between 2006 and 2013.

Future Matchup Plans and Division Context

Makhachev has expressed interest in fighting the winner of the upcoming interim welterweight title bout between Carlos Prates and Michael Morales. That interim bout is scheduled for January 30, 2027, as the co-main event of UFC 336 in Toronto, Canada.

  • Challenger Interest: Makhachev stated a desire to test himself against the winner to "prove to the world once again who is the best."
  • Scheduling Factors: UFC CEO Dana White stated earlier in the month that Makhachev was originally slated to defend his title in January, but chose to wait until after the Muslim holy month of Ramadan, which spans February and early March in 2027.
  • Promoter Perspective: White noted in a media conference that fighters cannot hold up divisions, making the interim bout between Prates and Morales a logical step for the organization.

Verification and Official Announcements

Observers can verify upcoming UFC schedules, event dates, and official championship updates by consulting the official UFC website or accredited sports news organizations. Fans should monitor verified social media handles belonging to the promotion and the athletes for direct announcements regarding fight confirmations and retirement timelines.
